readmodels.title: Course Catalogue
comments:
After 10 consecutive Ralph iterations flagged this as unresolved, determination: this is a leftover/incomplete duplicate of column D's "Course Catalogue" slice (d30964fa-e955-4edd-a3bb-25e956575b0d), not an intentional second consumer. Evidence: identical readmodel title/fields, but this node's inbound dependencies (Student Subscribed, Course Capacity Changed) are a strict subset of column D's (which also has Course Registered, Student Unsubscribed) — consistent with an earlier/partial version of the same model that was superseded when column D was completed. No specifications, commands, or screen were ever attached here. Building a second `/course-catalogue` route would collide with the one already implemented from column D.

Setting slice status to "Blocked" (rather than leaving it "Planned" forever) so the build loop stops re-picking an unbuildable stub. Recommended next step for a human modeler: delete this column/slice from the board, or explicitly wire up a distinct screen/actor if it truly is meant to be a second consumer.

This "Course Catalogue" read model (column G) duplicates the one in column D (both titled "Course Catalogue", and this one links back to the same node via data.linkedTo) but has no screen/actor connected here. Is this an intentional second consumer of the read model, or a leftover/incomplete duplicate that should be removed or merged into column D's slice?
